title: Validate the deployment horizon, not randomly shuffled rows
decision: Evaluate each candidate on deployment-length time windows; inspect variation and failure periods before choosing one forecast strategy.
applicability: Future observations are withheld in deployment; horizon and entity structure are known.
pitfalls: A lag that uses actual future targets during validation makes recursive inference look artificially strong.
The author also considered public LB in selection; transfer the time-window test, not unlimited public-LB tuning.
minimal_experiment: On fixed windows compare one recursive and one direct forecast. Record each window score, aggregate metric and end-to-end lag generation; keep training budget equal.

evidence.observation: The author used three adjacent 28-day validation windows and compared recursive/non-recursive forecasts across them.

title: Share entity-level splits and prediction identities across models
decision: Choose the deployment entity as the split boundary; retain entity IDs, row IDs and split versions when saving predictions for downstream blending.
applicability: Repeated observations belong to the same customer, essay, patient or recording.
pitfalls: HMS reports Group K-fold but the root post does not state the group-column name; verify code before claiming patient-level splitting.
An OOF filename does not establish that every row was predicted by a model that excluded that entity.
minimal_experiment: Generate a split manifest; check entity intersections and one-to-one ID joins for two prediction tables before testing their blend.

evidence.locator: Project Structure; Create unified kfold and holdout split
evidence.observation: The team aligned feature tables by customer UID and maintained common folds plus an independent customer holdout.
The team shared one verification procedure and used five-fold Group K-fold with a vote filter.

title: Turn repeated histories into structured feature families
decision: Start with grouped last/mean/variation and time-difference features; add families separately so improvements can be attributed.
applicability: Tabular prediction uses multiple ordered observations per entity.
pitfalls: Fitted encodings, selection and transformations must respect the validation boundary.
The author explored thousands of features with large resources; that scale is not a minimum requirement.
minimal_experiment: Compare last-observation baseline, aggregate family and temporal-difference family on the same entity folds; log memory, time and fold scores.

evidence.observation: Features included customer aggregates, differences, ratios, lags and type-specific transformations; the team then selected subsets.

title: Treat a faster proxy metric as a hypothesis
decision: Use the official metric for the target decision. If a cheap/stable proxy helps iteration, measure its agreement with the official metric on candidate runs.
applicability: The official metric is noisy or expensive and a proposed proxy has a plausible relationship.
pitfalls: The archive sometimes has blank or placeholder metric names; recover the actual formula from official evaluation documentation.
Proxy improvements alone do not establish a competition improvement.
minimal_experiment: Evaluate several existing predictions with both metrics; record ranking disagreements and only then decide whether the proxy is useful.

evidence.observation: The authors monitored the AMEX metric but used ROC AUC for many experiments because they considered AMEX unstable.

title: Judge a model by what it adds to the current ensemble
decision: Evaluate marginal ensemble gain on aligned held-out predictions instead of selecting solely by each model's individual score.
applicability: Multiple legal models produce predictions for the same held-out rows.
pitfalls: Ensemble weights can overfit the same validation set; separate weight fitting from evaluation where the existing competition workflow requires it.
A small single-model score loss may buy diversity, but diversity without measured gain is insufficient.
minimal_experiment: Add each candidate to one fixed base blend under the same weight-fitting procedure; record individual score, blend score and inference cost.

evidence.observation: Single-model scores did not reliably predict blend value; the team checked three-seed blends and complementary input formulations.
Recursive and non-recursive forecasts performed differently by period, motivating their combination.

title: Separate candidate coverage from candidate ranking
decision: Measure candidate recall before spending effort on the reranker; improve coverage with complementary retrieval sources.
applicability: The output chooses a small ranked set from a very large item catalog.
pitfalls: A reranker cannot recover a relevant item absent from its candidate set.
The reported candidate count and negative sampling rates reflect this author's hardware and data, not universal settings.
minimal_experiment: Compare revisit-only, plus covisitation and plus one embedding retriever at a fixed candidate budget. Measure candidate recall and final weighted recall separately.

evidence.observation: Candidates came from visited items, multiple covisitation matrices and neural retrieval; LGBM rankers then scored candidates.

title: Remove an information source from every stage in its ablation
decision: Define the unit of an ablation as an information source or decision, and remove all paths through which it reaches the output.
applicability: Features, retrieval, cached embeddings or auxiliary predictions are reused by several pipeline stages.
pitfalls: Removing only a final feature while leaving its candidates/cache intact understates dependence on that source.
minimal_experiment: Trace one shared signal through the pipeline, disable all its consumers and compare full-pipeline validation under the same split.

evidence.observation: When an information source fed both candidate generation and reranking, the authors removed it from both for the ablation.

title: Generate pseudo labels within the fold boundary
decision: Treat pseudo labels as model-derived artifacts with teacher training IDs and fold provenance; only use data permitted for the target competition.
applicability: Useful permitted unlabeled/weakly labeled data exist and teachers generalize to them.
pitfalls: A teacher trained on validation labels leaks those labels into its student even when the student never reads them directly.
More pseudo-label rounds are not automatically better; recheck gains and runtime.
minimal_experiment: Compare no pseudo labels and one fold-specific teacher round on unchanged folds; inspect quality and class coverage of the added examples.

evidence.observation: The team generated separate fold-safe and full-data pseudo-label versions for prior competition data.
Unlabeled soundscape pseudo labels helped; a high pseudo-label coefficient on training audio hurt.

title: Match audio context, label unit and prediction window
decision: Document how source recordings map to training windows, labels and submission rows; compare context schemes with identical boundary handling.
applicability: Audio labels are assigned to fixed windows while events cross window boundaries.
pitfalls: Overlapping windows from one recording must not cross train/validation boundaries.
CE training with sigmoid inference was specific to this report; do not treat it as a default multilabel recipe.
minimal_experiment: Compare one native-window baseline and one centered-context model; test short recordings and the first/last prediction windows.

evidence.locator: Model input; Postprocessing; What didn't work
evidence.observation: The authors trained on 10-second inputs built around 5-second label units and used matching context in inference; 10-second training with 5-second inference underperformed.

title: Audit data quality changes as model experiments
decision: Inspect duplicates and source quality, then evaluate each proposed filter separately with source and class coverage preserved.
applicability: Label noise, duplicated inputs or mismatched recording distributions are plausible.
pitfalls: A teacher-based filter can remove rare/hard true positives; record what was removed.
The author's favorable fold/signal-statistic choice is a retrospective report, not proof that choosing the easiest fold improves generalization.
minimal_experiment: Compare raw data, deduplication and one label-quality filter on fixed recording-group splits; examine per-class errors and retained counts.

evidence.observation: The team removed duplicate audio, filtered/reweighted some labels using a pretrained classifier, and reported failures for several extra-data choices.

title: Measure the complete inference pipeline before scaling models
decision: Profile preprocessing, model calls, postprocessing and startup separately; choose models by validation gain under the real hardware/time limit.
applicability: A code competition reruns inference under constrained runtime or CPU/GPU availability.
pitfalls: Cached preprocessing can trade time for memory; measure full test scale.
Author timings describe the historical environment and cannot establish current performance.
minimal_experiment: Run one realistic inference batch plus a full-size estimate on target hardware. Benchmark one cache/compiler change and verify prediction agreement.

evidence.observation: Fixed-shape OpenVINO, parallel spectrogram computation and cached mels supported CPU inference; slower alternative architectures did not improve their solution.

title: Compress an expensive ensemble into a soft-label student
decision: If the ensemble exceeds the inference budget, test a student against the teacher's held-out predictions and the official metric.
applicability: The teacher is strong, legal training inputs exist, and one smaller model can satisfy deployment constraints.
pitfalls: This source describes the efficiency prize, not a replacement rank-one main solution.
Student evaluation still needs entity-held-out labels; in-sample teacher predictions are not independent validation.
minimal_experiment: Train one student from fold-safe soft labels, compare it with teacher and hard-label student, and measure full inference time including tokenization.

evidence.observation: The efficiency-prize model learned from soft pseudo labels on prior data and OOF soft labels on train data; length-aware pretokenization further reduced runtime.

title: Localize anatomy before modeling severity
decision: For sparse targets in large images/volumes, compare a localization-plus-classification pipeline against a direct baseline.
applicability: Useful localized structures exist and downstream labels depend on a small part of a larger input.
pitfalls: Use held-out localization predictions for downstream validation; ground-truth crops hide stage-one errors.
This competition evidence establishes no clinical diagnosis or clinical validation.
minimal_experiment: Freeze one localizer, generate held-out crops and compare mean pooling with one MIL head under the same study splits.

evidence.observation: Slice/coordinate prediction created crops for downstream severity models; MIL and bi-LSTM aggregated the resulting image instances.

title: Train the downstream stage on realistic upstream errors
decision: Estimate upstream error from held-out predictions and reproduce its plausible range during downstream training.
applicability: A model consumes coordinates, retrieval results or features estimated by another model.
pitfalls: Arbitrary perturbations can produce unrealistic samples; large offsets may erase the target.
Estimate error without validation-label contamination in the final comparison.
minimal_experiment: Compare no perturbation and measured-error perturbation, stratifying downstream score by localization-error size.

evidence.observation: The author perturbed coordinates and slice indices, with slice-shift probability tied to observed localization errors.

title: Combine embedding retrieval with classification for unseen identities
decision: For identity matching, evaluate known and unseen identities separately and compare embedding retrieval with classifier scores.
applicability: The test can include identities absent from training, and the metric scores ranked identity candidates.
pitfalls: The author tuned unknown-frequency thresholds using submissions; that frequency is not a transferable constant.
KNN and classifier calibration can vary with per-identity sample count and train/test shift.
minimal_experiment: Hold out some identities entirely, compare KNN/classifier/blend and select the unknown threshold on held-out identities.

evidence.observation: Sub-center ArcFace embeddings supported KNN retrieval; classifier outputs were blended and low-confidence cases were labeled new_individual.

title: Maintain a frozen opponent pool and test both perspectives
decision: Use opponent diversity to reveal policy regressions; verify observation/action transforms for both player positions.
applicability: A legal game agent is evaluated against evolving opponents in a symmetric or transformable environment.
pitfalls: An opponent used for training is not an independent test opponent.
The reported billions of training steps are historical resource use, not a prerequisite for this pattern.
minimal_experiment: Evaluate current and candidate policies against frozen opponents on identical seeds in both positions; record W/L/T, illegal actions and timeouts.

evidence.observation: The authors mixed self-play with frozen older/teacher opponents and normalized player perspective with coordinate transforms.

title: Use a measured fallback when expensive test-time augmentation runs out of budget
decision: Profile per-step and accumulated inference cost; add a fallback whose actions are still legal when the expensive path is skipped.
applicability: The environment has per-step or cumulative execution limits and an optional expensive policy step.
pitfalls: The historical 30-second trigger depends on that environment; compute a threshold from current limits.
A fallback must not leave stale recurrent state or untransformed actions.
minimal_experiment: Force the fallback threshold in local matches; verify legality and state transitions while comparing timeout rate and win rate.

evidence.observation: The authors disabled flip-based inference augmentation when accumulated overtime exceeded a threshold.

title: Reformulate alignment as a probability grid with domain channels
decision: When targets represent alignment or trajectories, test a structured probability representation and a simple expected-path decoder before making the backbone larger.
applicability: A reference sequence and target sequence have physically meaningful alignment coordinates.
pitfalls: Grid range/resolution can truncate valid paths; inspect boundary errors.
PF and neighbor channels require independent generation for held-out wells; preserved physical constraints do not guarantee label correctness.
minimal_experiment: On fixed well splits compare direct regression and a coarse alignment grid. Add one domain channel; report official metric and boundary/outlier cases.

evidence.locator: Task Formulation and Loss; Features; Data Augmentation
evidence.observation: The author predicted a typewell-by-horizontal-well probability map, with cross entropy plus expected-path/domain losses and PF/neighbor channels.

title: Route auxiliary models by measured feature reliability
decision: Analyze disagreement by subgroup and data coverage before dropping a locally useful signal; compare a reliability-aware blend with a global blend.
applicability: An auxiliary data source is missing, sparse or shifted for identifiable examples.
pitfalls: The author attributed remaining disagreement to inconsistent labels; that attribution is an author hypothesis, not a verified cause.
A standalone feature gain may disappear in the strongest single model yet add ensemble diversity.
minimal_experiment: Define reliability from input-only statistics, fit routing within training folds, then evaluate global versus gated blend on held-out wells.

evidence.locator: XY Neighbor Information; Ensemble; What didn't work
evidence.observation: Neighbor features improved local CV but hurt public LB; the author investigated neighborhood statistics and used models without neighbors where that information was unreliable.

title: Investigate the data-generating mechanism before adding model complexity
decision: When inputs were produced by a documented process, test its equations and residuals as a separate hypothesis with a fallback model.
applicability: The competition data generator is documented and its permitted inputs identify a stable relationship.
pitfalls: Matching may exploit benchmark-specific simulation artifacts and need not transfer to real data.
Do not seek hidden labels or use an unpermitted source; confirm the competition rules for the proposed mechanism.
minimal_experiment: Test a small labeled training subset against the forward process; report coverage, error on matched/unmatched groups and sensitivity to added noise.

evidence.locator: Deep Learning Models; Matching data with PID controllers
evidence.observation: The authors combined deep sequence models with reconstruction of the simulated controller, finding exact matches for a portion of the benchmark.

title: Combine local improvement with perturbations and an exact scorer
decision: Use cheap screening to allocate exact evaluations while retaining the official scorer as the acceptance criterion.
applicability: The solution is a valid discrete configuration/permutation and exact scoring is expensive.
pitfalls: Surrogate error can discard useful candidates; reserve some exact evaluations for calibration/exploration.
Repository has no declared license; use the documented idea and original implementation unless reuse is permitted.
minimal_experiment: Under equal exact-evaluation budgets compare local search and perturbation-assisted search, then test one surrogate screen; checkpoint the best valid solution.

evidence.observation: The author code README describes iterated local search, kicks, depth-first neighborhood exploration and lightweight neural pruning before expensive exact scoring.
